lines.en: [Main Scenario # 3 ― Emergency Defense has ended.]
[You have earned 1000 coins as a reward.]
The main scenario I had thought would only begin once the sun was high in the sky was already showing signs of starting, damn it, less than 10 minutes after the third main scenario ended.
[The fourth main scenario will begin shortly!]
Damn it, the third one had barely ended, and already······.
I went straight over to Lee Jihye.
“Stay here with Yoo Joonghyuk.”
“······Is that okay?”
“Going down now wouldn't help anyway. And if that bastard wakes up, that'll be a problem in itself.”
Lee Jihye nodded, looking at Yoo Joonghyuk, who was still unconscious.
“Just let me know when he wakes up. I'll give him another smack on the back of the head.”
With that, I headed downstairs with Jung Heewon. Lee Gilyoung had fallen fast asleep while counting the meteors, so I decided to carry him down on my back.

The place where the dungeon had been was now an ordinary theatre, and the items in the fifth-floor reward dungeon had turned into ordinary stage props. As though everything that had happened yesterday had been a dream.
That was when I heard Bihyung's voice.
[······You know what I'm going to say, right?]
‘Yeah.’
[Whew······ You nearly scared me to death, seriously.]
Hearing Bihyung grumble put me a little at ease.

Constellations possessed tremendous power and wealth, but they were by no means omniscient (全知). All the sound and images from the scenarios had to reach them through a dokkaebi's ‘channel.’ In other words, what that meant was—
‘Did the filtering work properly? I got worked up and said far too much unnecessary stuff.’
[Of course it did. You think I'd let my channel go under? Information at that level gets filtered automatically.]
If I was right, what I had said to Yoo Joonghyuk had probably reached the constellations like this.
―Do you really think that? Have you already forgotten the resolve you had when you first ■■?
―How are you alone? Even when you ■■■■■■■■ like an idiot, even when you clutched ■■■■ and whined, ■■■■■■! Even when you first ■■ with the person you loved!
―Helping ■■■, fighting against ■■■! Even when you finally stood ■■■ ■■!
I didn't know how heavily it had actually been filtered.

Whatever the case, it would have been more heavily filtered than this, if anything, certainly no less. I remembered seeing information blocked this way in the early stages of the original novel, even when word began to spread that Yoo Joonghyuk was a ‘regressor.’
[Don't worry. The constellations won't have heard a thing. The problem is, I didn't hear much either······.]
‘······You couldn't hear it either?’
That was a little strange. Was there information even a dokkaebi couldn't hear?
[That's right, you punk. What the hell were you talking about?]
Information even a dokkaebi hadn't heard. One possibility did come to mind.
Could it be······ the restrictions of ‘probability’ were already starting to take effect?
A passage from ‘Ways of Survival’ naturally came to mind.
「<Probability> is a vast restraining force that controls the flow of the Star Stream.」
······It came to mind, but it wasn't much help right now.
One reason Ways of Survival had flopped was that it had far too many elements of its setting that even the author probably didn't understand.
‘How are the other constellations reacting?’
[They're raising hell. They're still making a huge fuss, demanding to know what you said.]
Of course they were. For the constellations whose feed had been filtered, it was as though a talking picture had suddenly turned into a silent film.

Still, the smart constellations would have begun to focus on my potential instead of complaining to the Bureau. The fact that my words had been filtered meant, conversely, that I knew information that shouldn't be revealed at this point.
[A small number of constellations who investigate secrets are taking notice of your existence.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ finds your existence intriguing]
[You have received 2000 coins in sponsorship.]
Bihyung added, as though he had just remembered something.
[There were so many indirect messages earlier that I didn't forward them to you individually. You know that, right?]
‘Keep doing that. Only show messages from the ones who say they'll pay a lot of coins.’
[······What am I, your manager?]
Looking slightly sulky, Bihyung soon vanished from the air.
Somehow, that little guy seemed to get cuter as time went on.
That took care of one thing. The other was······.
“Dokja-ssi, aren't you tired? Let me carry Gilyoung.”
“Ah, I'd appreciate that.”
I handed Lee Gilyoung over to Jung Heewon. There was something serious about her expression. After a little hesitation, I spoke.
“Heewon-ssi.”
“Yes?”
“Something's on your mind, isn't it?”
“No, it's just······.”
Jung Heewon hesitated for a moment, then sighed.
“Hah······ All right. I'm just not the type to keep this bottled up.”
As expected.
Jung Heewon went straight for it without beating around the bush.
“Dokja-ssi, who exactly are you?”
“···Did you hear something earlier?”
“A little.”

We had been quite far apart, so I had thought she wouldn't hear, but unfortunately, it seemed she had heard something. Then again, Jung Heewon had been closer than Lee Jihye, and speech between humans wasn't filtered······.
I could hear Lee Gilyoung snoring softly.
I decided to be only half honest.
“I know part of the future.”
“Is that true?”
“Yes.”
Jung Heewon seemed to consider something for a moment. She appeared to be weighing whether my words were true. Then, at some point, she bit her lip, as though she had made up her mind.
“Does Yoo Sangah-ssi or Lee Hyunsung-ssi know?”
“Not yet.”
When I answered readily, Jung Heewon took hesitant steps away from me with Lee Gilyoung still on her back.
“······You're not going to suddenly kill us or anything, are you?”
“Why would you suddenly say that?”
“That's usually how these things go. ‘You know too much about me,’ that sort of thing······.”
Where on earth had she gotten this ‘usual turn of events’? Somehow, I felt like I had become a terrible person.
“I don't know what you mean by the ‘usual turn of events,’ but if that were how it worked, I think I would have killed you and the others already.”
“Actually, that part does seem a little strange.”
“······I didn't bring this up with bad intentions. Quite the opposite.”
“The opposite?”
I looked into Jung Heewon's eyes as I spoke.
“The scenarios ahead will be more dangerous. We'll have to escape death time and again, and we may lose things precious to us.”
Watching the growing anxiety in Jung Heewon's eyes, I continued.
“Please continue to stay by my side.”
“······What do you mean?”
“I'm asking you to become my ‘companion.’”
It was about time I began gathering ‘my own people.’
‘People I could trust,’ who at least wouldn't betray me easily.
Jung Heewon, whom I had awakened and whose mind I could read, was the best candidate for that. After looking stunned for a moment, her lips twitched.
“So you've never thought of me as a companion before, Dokja-ssi?”
“To be precise, it's the opposite. We don't become companions just because I think we are.”
Jung Heewon's gaze wavered faintly.
I deliberately took a step back.

“If being companions feels like too much, you can think of it as a deal. I need your fighting strength, and my information will help you. We each give and receive something. What matters is that our relationship stays the same from now on.”
“This is a little sudden... Do I have to answer right now?”
“No.”
With someone like Jung Heewon, a patient approach was more likely to win her over than hastily playing on her emotions.
In fact, Jung Heewon didn't look particularly displeased.
[The character ‘Jung Heewon’ is reassured by your honesty.]
[The character ‘Jung Heewon’ begins to consider your proposal seriously.]
She probably wouldn't agonize over it for long. Since I had played such a large part in her awakening event, my presence would be deeply imprinted on her subconscious.
The second <Sponsor Selection> would probably begin once this scenario ended.
Then Jung Heewon would finally gain a constellation sponsor, too. That was when her true potential would begin to emerge.
“Then can I ask one more thing?”
“Yes.”
“What am I doing in the ‘future’ you know, Dokja-ssi?”
I looked up into the air.
This was being filtered properly, right?
“I don't know either.”
“···What?”
“Because you weren't in the future I knew, Jung Heewon-ssi.”
“What does that······.”
“That's why you need this deal.”
Jung Heewon's eyes widened.
Jung Heewon was a variable I had cultivated myself, someone who hadn't received attention in the original novel.
Her attributes were more than sufficient. Now, if she gained the right constellation sponsor, she would be able to play a key role in changing the scenarios ahead.
Especially when we fought bastards with ‘other variables’ I knew nothing about.
That was when I heard a commotion downstairs.
“Think it over carefully. Let's hurry a little.”
We practically flew over the ticket gates and down to the platform, where a large group had surrounded a handful of people and was pressuring them.
I quickly understood what was happening.
The Landlord Alliance.
Apparently, they still hadn't learned their lesson.
“Where'd that bastard Kim Dokja go? Hurry up and tell us!”
Looking closer, I spotted Lee Hyunsung among the alliance members, looking troubled.
I approached them, deliberately making my footsteps loud.
“Lee Hyunsung-ssi, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“It's him!”
The moment I came down onto the Line 4 platform, someone in the alliance shouted.
I could see the landlord with the familiar face.
Traces of the fierce battle he had fought all night remained all over his body. Even at a glance, I could tell his overall stats had risen substantially. I liked what I saw.
“Gong Pildu.”

A full eight miniature turrets rose from the [Armed Zone] of the glaring Gong Pildu. Rallying around him, the alliance members looked at me with renewed confidence. Ungrateful even after I'd saved their lives. People really were a treacherous lot.
“That bastard, right now······!”
Gong Pildu was about to say something when he suddenly flinched.
Electricity was crackling through the air.
[The fourth main scenario will begin in 5 minutes!]
Along with the system message, the dokkaebi Bihyung appeared.
[Hahaha, everyone, have you been well?]
At the malicious little bastard's voice, everyone's faces hardened.
[Judging by your expressions, you all seem to have been doing splendidly!]
“Wh-what are you here for!”
[For the fourth main scenario announcement, of course.]
“Fucking hell······.”

[Now, now, don't get so worked up. Listen. You know the biggest complainers are the first to croak, right? For the fourth main scenario, you'll be joining the other stations. A very exciting story awaits, so I'm sure you'll all be thoroughly satisfied!]
At the mention of joining the other stations, everyone's faces grew even darker.
Chungmuro alone had turned out like this. It was obvious how much of a mess things would become once other stations got involved. Bihyung snickered.

[But before you can proceed with this scenario, you must complete a preliminary task. Simply adding more people would only create chaos, wouldn't it? So you need someone to lead you. In other words, your station needs a <representative>!]
A representative. So it was finally beginning.
[That means the game you'll be playing now is a ‘preliminary round.’ You could call it a warm-up game, too. As for the rules······ well, you'll understand when you see them!]
Bihyung vanished with a sinister smile, and a message window appeared before everyone.
[A sub-scenario has arrived!]
<Sub-scenario ― Elect a Representative>
Category : Sub
Difficulty : C
Clear Conditions : Take possession of the ‘white flag’ installed at the center of the platform.
Time Limit : 30 minutes
Reward : 1000 coins, representative of Chungmuro.
Failure : ―
●The station's representative can exercise powerful control over its members.

Before the message window had even fully appeared, Gong Pildu had already deactivated his Armed Zone and was running toward the flag at the center of the platform. Sure enough, the bastard was uncannily quick on the uptake.
“Everyone, get lost!”
Shoving people aside like a runaway train, Gong Pildu was already in front of the white flag.
I wasn't about to let that happen.
Just as his thick fingers were about to touch the flag, I spoke.
“Gong Pildu, get down!”
[‘Command rights’ activate under the terms of the contract!]
“Uwaaagh!”
I lightly stepped on Gong Pildu's back as he collapsed, leaped up, and took the ‘white flag.’
[You have pulled the ‘white flag’ from the flag holder.]
[You have become the ‘representative’ of Chungmuro Station.]
[You have qualified to walk the ‘King’s Road.’]
The moment the flag wound around my hand, I felt powerful energy surge through my body. It was supposed to belong to the Yoo Joonghyuk of the third round, but······ it probably wouldn't matter.
That bastard was already strong, wasn't he?
[‘Kim Dokja’ has taken possession of the ‘white flag.’]
[If ownership of the white flag remains unchanged for the next 5 minutes, Chungmuro Station will come under his control.]
[Seizing the flag changes its owner and resets the 5-minute timer.]
A timer then appeared in the air.
Gong Pildu went pale and pointed at me.
“Take the flag! We just have to take it within 5 minutes!”
The alliance members finally came to their senses and rushed toward me.
Oh, so that was how they wanted to play?
Lee Hyunsung looked at me.
“Dokja-ssi!”
“Hyunsung-ssi!”
We called to each other at the same time. [Hercules’ Shield] flew from my hand and settled snugly into Lee Hyunsung's.
“Wh-what's this?”
“I picked out a nice one for you. Throw away the one you were using.”
A huge grin spread across Lee Hyunsung's face.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ activates the special skill ‘Wide-area Defense’!]
A translucent barrier spread out from Hercules’ Shield, enclosing our party in a small space.
Sure enough, once an item reached A-grade, it came with a useful auxiliary skill.
“Whoa, what's this!”

People groaned as they collided with the barrier that had appeared in midair. They banged on it with their old weapons, but there was no way mere E-grade or F-grade equipment could break it. In the end, there was only one person the alliance members could turn to.
“Pildu-ssi!”
“Everyone, move!”

Perhaps his [Armed Zone] level had risen considerably in the meantime; a small Armed Zone was already spreading beneath Gong Pildu's feet. He seemed to be trying to shorten the cooldown by limiting its area. Pretty clever.
It looked like I'd have to put him through his paces properly before he'd learn his lesson.
“Pildu, I haven't told you to get up yet, have I?”
“Urgh?”
Gong Pildu slammed his head into the floor with a bang and flattened himself against it again.
[‘Command rights’ activate under the terms of the contract!]
“Keep your head planted on the floor until I tell you to get up.”
At Gong Pildu's scream, the flustered alliance members shouted.
“P-Pildu-ssi?!”
“G-get me up! Hurry!”
The alliance members crowded around and frantically tried to raise Gong Pildu, but perhaps because he was so big, they didn't seem to be having much luck.
“And······ those turrets are getting on my nerves, so turn them off.”
[The ‘Armed Zone Lv.6’ of the character ‘Gong Pildu’ is deactivated.]
“Y-you son of a······!”
“Shut that filthy mouth of yours, too. Take a vow of silence for 30 minutes.”
[‘Command rights’ activate under the terms of the contract!]
“Mmph mmph mmph mmph mmph!”

With Gong Pildu, the man they had relied on, rendered helpless by just a few words, the Landlord Alliance members looked utterly panicked. Of course, my companions—including Lee Hyunsung, Yoo Sangah, and Jung Heewon—were just as surprised. I grinned and spoke.
“Now, it seems everyone understands the situation. I'd like to have a little talk······.”
I could see people backing away hesitantly.
A rough count put the total number remaining at twenty-nine.

Twenty were Landlord Alliance members, and the other nine were the smaller group that included me and my companions. It wasn't a large number, but I thought that might be for the best. Too many people from the outset would be difficult to manage. I looked at them and said,
“You now have two choices.”
It was time to find out who was on our side.
“One is to leave Chungmuro and go to another station. Two is to stay here with me.”
“Wh-what are you suddenly······.”
“Just answer. Will you stay here, or will you go somewhere else? You'd better decide before the main scenario starts. Otherwise, all your lives will be in danger.”
Their eyes began to dart about. Some looked at me, some at Gong Pildu, and some at the tunnels leading to other stations. Sometimes, a glance was enough to tell what someone was thinking.
“I won't stop anyone determined to leave. But if you stay here, you'll all have to follow my orders.”
“Orders······?”
“I will no longer tolerate behavior like that of the ‘Landlord Alliance.’ Nor will I allow a small group to abuse its power.”

The few people who had been quietly watching began to move to my side, one by one. Having suffered badly at the hands of the Landlord Alliance, they probably thought siding with me would be better. A good decision. Several alliance members shouted.
“In the end, you just want to play king!”
“I won't deny it. But I won't collect taxes or survival fees like certain people.”
“If we join your group, will our safety be guaranteed?”
One of the men who had belonged to the alliance asked. Well, after tormenting their tenants so much, it made sense that they would worry about that.
“I'll guarantee a degree of protection from outside threats, but I won't interfere in matters within the group. You'll have to settle disputes between individuals yourselves.”
“B-but that's······.”
“I'll give you 1 minute. Everyone, decide by then.”

There was no need to wait the full minute. Everyone already looked as though they had made up their minds. A few alliance members approached me and bowed their heads, seemingly resolved. They were among the younger ones.
“We look forward to working with you. We have done wrong in the past, but we ask that you generously forgive us.”
“Likewise. Though I'm not the one you should be asking for forgiveness.”
[Some members of the group show trust in you.]
A few others, however, seemed to have decided to leave Chungmuro after all.
They tried to lift the fallen Gong Pildu and get him moving somehow.
I looked at them and said,
“Ah, leave Gong Pildu here. He belongs to me.”
“What do you mean······!”
“If you've decided, hurry up and leave.”
At my cold declaration, five alliance members stepped back, scowling.
“Kang-ssi! You're really not coming with us? Nothing good will come of staying under that bastard!”
“Come on, everyone! Are you really going to live as that bastard's lackeys? You saw what he's like!”
But no one else left.

The five men swore, looked back at us several times with lingering reluctance, and then headed into the tunnel toward Myeongdong. They probably intended to settle somewhere else and become ‘landlords’ again, but unfortunately, their plan would fail. In the fourth scenario, ‘wanderers’ like them were easy prey for predators.
Just then, apparently marking the end of the 5 minutes, a system message appeared.
[The sub-scenario has ended.]
[You have received 1000 coins as a reward.]
[Through the effect of the white flag, you have become the true ‘representative’ of Chungmuro Station.]
[Your current group : 24 members]
[Your renown is still insufficient to gain the title of king.]
The title of king······.
Well, it would be difficult to earn the title of ‘king’ with a white flag.
To truly walk the ‘King’s Road,’ I would have to keep changing the color of my flag.
Of course, white had its own ‘authority,’ too.
[Through the effect of the white flag, you have gained control over the Chungmuro group.]
[You can inflict ‘punishment’ on group members who defy you.]
[5 members have now deserted.]
I considered giving the departing men a little demonstration of ‘punishment,’ then decided against it. Rule through fear was effective for controlling people, but that sort of tyranny didn't suit me.
“Then I look forward to working with you.”
I spoke while meeting each person's eyes.
Lee Hyunsung was looking at me with respect, while Yoo Sangah and Jung Heewon nodded.
Everyone else wore much the same expression as they watched one another for cues.
They were still a disorganized rabble, but this wasn't a bad start.
A moment later, Bihyung appeared in the air.
[Oho, you've chosen a representative. Then let's get into the real game!]
[The fourth main scenario has been activated!]
<Main Scenario # 4 ― Struggle for the Flag >
Category : Main
Difficulty : C
Clear Conditions : (The window is hidden due to the large amount of content)
Time Limit : 12 days
Reward : 2000 coins
Failure : ???
I tapped the clear conditions.
A lengthy message appeared before my eyes.
[Clear Conditions]
1.Every station has a ‘flag’ that can be used to occupy a ‘flag holder.’
2.Only the station's ‘representative’ may carry its flag.

3.You must defend your ‘flag holder’ from groups belonging to other stations. If another group's flag is planted in your station's ‘flag holder,’ you will lose the station. The treatment of the group that loses its station will be determined by the group occupying the ‘flag holder.’

4.You may plant your ‘flag’ in another station's ‘flag holder.’ Only each station's ‘representative’ has the authority to plant the flag. If the representative dies in an armed clash during this process, the authority of ‘representative’ will pass to the first person to pick up the flag. If another station's group seizes your ‘flag,’ the treatment of the group that loses its flag will be determined by the group that seizes it.
5.You must occupy the ‘flag holder’ of your ‘target station’ within the allotted time. If you fail, every member of your group will die.
6.The ‘target station’ your group must occupy is [Changsin Station].
Jung Heewon seemed to think for a moment, then spoke.
“······It sounds like it's telling us to protect our flag and flag holder while planting our flag in another station. Have I understood that right?”
“That's how I understood it, too. And Changsin Station is where we need to plant our flag.”
Lee Hyunsung added his thoughts. Then I spoke.
“That seems to be it. You all have a good grasp of it.”
At my words, Jung Heewon gave me a sidelong glare.
As if to ask why I was playing dumb when I knew everything.
Well, now that she knew I knew the future, I probably did seem irritating. I grinned at her.
Yoo Sangah clasped her shoulders and spoke.
“Do we have to······ fight people again?”
After thinking for a moment, Lee Hyunsung answered.
“It says that once we occupy a station's ‘flag holder,’ we can decide how its group members are treated······ so if we handle things well, we may be able to avoid casualties.”
“Oh, you're right. It doesn't say that losing a station means dying immediately, does it? If we could take in that station's group members when deciding how to treat them······.”
“Yes, we might be able to clear it without anyone dying.”
Lee Hyunsung answered with a smile, but watching him left me uneasy.
Sometimes, Yoo Sangah and Lee Hyunsung seemed to be trying to understand the world through some sort of heavenly logic.
There was no such thing as a scenario in which no one died.
The fourth scenario would produce more casualties than any scenario so far.
As though she understood how I felt, Jung Heewon interrupted with a slight frown.
“What line is Changsin Station on? I think we need to find that out first.”
Lee Hyunsung checked the route map and spoke.
“Line 6. If we travel only through the tunnels, we could go around through Yaksu and use the transfer passage······.”
“Then we'll have to split the group. How about some of us stay to guard this place, while the others go scout that way?”
Watching my companions actively exchange ideas without any prompting from me left me feeling strangely pleased.
[The activation of the scenario removes the protective barrier around ‘Chungmuro Station.’]
[You may now travel freely between stations.]
While my companions exchanged their ideas, I approached Gong Pildu.
“Gong Pildu, you can talk now.”
But even with the order lifted, Gong Pildu merely ground his teeth at me and was slow to speak.
“I know you have a grudge against me. But you need to adapt, too. Your days as a landlord are over.”
“I know why you're so obsessed with ‘land.’ But rein it in, if you want to keep surviving. You have something you need to do, don't you?”
Gong Pildu's wavering gaze. I continued.
“You'll be in charge of guarding this place.”

Gong Pildu was a very useful piece in the fourth scenario as well as the third. At least, as long as he guarded this place, Chungmuro would be safe unless some lunatic on Yoo Joonghyuk's level showed up.
“Why should I listen to a bastard like you······.”
“I won't force you with an order this time. And if you do as I ask, you'll be rewarded accordingly.”
“Think it over carefully. Think about the family you're separated from, too.”
At my last words, Gong Pildu's eyes widened.
“You, how did you······!”
That was when a noise came from the tunnel.
Hooonk―!
Along with a loud horn, headlights shone along the Line 4 tracks leading to Dongdaemun History and Culture Park.
The sound of motorcycle engines, and the acrid roar of exhaust.
Something was approaching Chungmuro.
······Already? The scenario had barely started.

I recalled the original novel, but I didn't remember the invasions beginning this quickly. It meant a variable had appeared. Soon, the headlights went out in the darkness, and I heard people murmuring.
“Ah, Chungmuro's finally opened up.”
“Seriously, they took forever just to clear a scenario like that.”
“Hey, keep it down. They'll hear everything. And don't you know the scenarios differ from station to station?”
At a glance from me, my companions rose with their weapons in hand.
What mattered in a fight was securing your position first.
I took the lead, followed by Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon, with Yoo Sangah bringing up the rear. Lee Gilyoung was still asleep, so we left him there.
Had a few seconds passed? I saw four people, men and women, walking toward us out of the darkness. I spoke.
“Stop right there.”
“Oh? Well, well.”
Startled at the blade I pointed at him, the man stopped in his tracks. I could make out the white, gleaming body of a motorcycle. I heard weapons being drawn in the darkness, but the man spoke first.
“Wait a moment. Let's all calm down. Goodness, you're scaring me so much I can hardly talk.”
“Put down your weapons and come this way slowly.”

The man readily set his weapon on the ground and approached with both hands raised. Once I saw him in the light, he didn't look particularly unpleasant. A reasonably likable face. His narrow eyes curved into gentle arcs.
“Please don't be so wary. We haven't come to fight.”
“Then what have you come for?”
“First, let me introduce myself. My name is Kang Ilhun, and I'm the deputy representative of the ‘Dongdaemun group.’”
Kang Ilhun? As expected, he wasn't someone who immediately came to mind.
And Dongdaemun's deputy representative······ Something about this was taking a strange turn.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
Since the skill worked, it seemed certain that he was a character from the novel, at least.
<Character Information>
Name : Kang Ilhun
Age : 31
Constellation Sponsor (背後星) : Shameless Good Gossiper
Exclusive Attribute : Rumours Expert (General)
Exclusive Skills : [Weapons Training Lv.2], [Art of Communication Lv.3], [Spread Rumours Lv.1]
Stigma : [Making a Commotion Lv.1]
Overall Stats : [Constitution Lv.12], [Strength Lv.13], [Agility Lv.13], [Magic Power Lv.10]

Overall Evaluation : Unfortunately, he has failed to blossom due to ending up with the wrong constellation sponsor, but his stats are respectable enough for use as an ordinary soldier. Caution is advised, as he spreads rumors without distinguishing truth from falsehood.
A Rumours Expert······.
Was it already time for bastards like him to start running rampant?
Kang Ilhun looked at me with a hint of anxiety.
“And your name is······?”
“Kim Dokja.”
“Ah, Kim Dokja-ssi······?”
At my name, a puzzled look briefly crossed Kang Ilhun's face.
But it lasted only an instant.
“A pleasure to meet you, Kim Dokja-ssi. Since you have the flag, I take it you're the station's representative?”
“That's right.”

He studied my appearance, then swept his gaze over the companions around me. He was probably assessing our fighting strength. The bastard had a good eye, but unfortunately, he'd picked the wrong opponent.
“If you're done looking, let's get to the point.”
“Haha. My apologies. We have to consider our safety, too.”
Kang Ilhun continued without losing his composure.
“As I said, we haven't come to fight. How should I put it? Perhaps you could say we've come to make you a ‘good offer.’”
I examined the appearance of Kang Ilhun's companions.
None of them seemed to be carrying a flag.
“How can I believe that?”

“Hmm, you should know if you've checked the rules. If we'd come to fight, we would have brought our representative. Only each station's representative can plant a flag in the ‘flag holder,’ after all.”
That was true. It was certainly true, but—
“What's your offer?”
“We've come to request an alliance.”
At the word ‘alliance,’ the Chungmuro group members began to murmur.
Kang Ilhun launched into his genial patter.
“Ah, since Chungmuro Station has only just opened, you probably don't know. The ‘fourth scenario’ has actually been underway for two days already.”
“···Two days?”
Yoo Sangah murmured reflexively. Kang Ilhun nodded.
“Yes, the content and duration of the third scenario differ slightly from station to station······ Didn't you know?”
The third scenario had only just ended. There was no way they could have known that. In the original novel, too, Chungmuro entered the scenario later than the other stations.
In other words, we were starting at something of an informational disadvantage.
In that sense, Kang Ilhun's proposal of an alliance was an undeniably timely temptation.
We needed information, and they needed our strength.
The question was what sinister scheme they had in mind.
“It's not an offer I can readily accept. We have no way of knowing if you have some ulterior motive.”
